text: Specifying a representation of $G$ on $V$ over $k$ is the same data as making $V$ a module over:
explanation: The key insight of the chapter is that a representation is exactly a left $k[G]$-module, via $g\cdot v=\rho(g)(v)$. Every vector space is already a $k$-module, so that choice carries no group data; $GL(V)$ is a group, not a ring to take modules over; and $\mathrm{End}_k(V)$ is the target of the associated ring homomorphism, not the ring $V$ is a module over here.
